feature: The Layers list says how many picked layers are inside copies
summary: When a selection reaches inside copies of a component, the line under the Layers list now says so: "4 layers selected, 2 inside a copy". Before this it said "4 layers selected" over two highlighted rows and left you to work out where the other two were.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Components and saved colours are on by default; no flag to find.

try.do: Open Library, press Save Colour, and name it Accent.
Draw a second rectangle, sweep both, and press Command G.
Make it a component, then drag one copy of it out of the Comps shelf.
Open Library, pick Accent, and press Select What Uses This.
Read the line under the Layers list: it should say 4 layers selected, 2 inside a copy.
Click any single layer, then shift-click a second one, and check the line goes back to plain "2 layers selected".

evaluate: Does "2 inside a copy" tell you where the missing highlights went, or does it raise a new question?
Is "a copy" the word you would use for what the shelf drops on the canvas?
The line sits under the list, quiet and to the right. Is that where your eye goes when the count and the highlights disagree?
Would you rather the list took you to those pieces than told you about them?
A layer inside a SHUT group is not counted here, because a twist brings its row back. Is that the right line to draw?
rough: The decision asked for a second short line; this is one line with a clause on the end instead. It says both numbers, it never truncates (the longest version measures 170pt in a 236pt space), and it costs the panel no extra height. Changing it back to two lines is a small edit if you want the separation.

The picture above is a real capture of the window, but the Mac reported its screen LOCKED for this whole task, so every walk refused to run and this one was forced through with PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1. The harness says a run in that state is not a verdict, so treat the picture as what it is, a photograph, and not as a passing walk. A sweep is already pending and re-runs the walk once the screen is unlocked.

The line tells you those pieces are picked but gives you no way to get to them: there is no row to click, and nothing scrolls anywhere. If that turns out to be the thing you want, it is a separate feature (reveal the copy, or open the original).

Two pieces inside ONE copy read as "2 inside a copy" and pieces spread over two copies read as "2 inside copies". That is a real difference and it is carried by one word, which may be too quiet to notice.
